label: Having a perfection in an agent's power is a more perfect mode than every other way of having it
paraphrase: Analyst formulation of the strong comparand of the q.4 a.2 first proof's mode step: for the primitive comparison of modes ModeAbove, the virtual mode (in an agent's power) is above every other way of having a perfection, the effect's formal possession ('secundum eandem rationem') included. It extends the passage's 'eminentiori modo', said of the equivocal agent's possession compared with the effect's, to the virtual mode as such; that extension is an unattributed analyst step. The modes are not exclusive: a univocal agent has its effect's perfection both formally and in its power. It compares modes, not bearers; no statement relates it to the eminent comparative of bearers proposed in PR #2166 (MORE_4), and it does not say that the agent has the perfection intrinsically. The passage applies 'eminentiori modo' to the sun. Open.

connection_plan.missing_bridge: A bridge from the strong mode comparison to intrinsic possession of a pure perfection at an actual root: that having a perfection virtually, in a mode above the effect's formal possession, is a way of really having it.
connection_plan.blocker: The passage attributes the eminent mode to the sun, an impersonal agent, so a mode ranking above formal possession does not by itself give intrinsic possession; the intrinsic-perfection obligations (E and L, causal-perfection-transfer 2026-11-24) and the second proof's subsistent-esse premises carry that content and remain open.
